beats.label: S1 · The mission
beats.text: In 2166 immortal warlord Vandal Savage rules the world. Time Master Rip Hunter steals a timeship to recruit eight misfits from 2016 to kill Savage before his rise.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Establishes the entire premise — Rip's motivation, Savage as villain, and the assembled team.

beats.label: S1 · Chronos is Mick
beats.text: Hunting them across time is Chronos — revealed as Mick himself, whom Snart tried to kill before the Time Masters captured and reprogrammed him into their bounty hunter.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Fractures the Snart-Mick partnership and marks the Time Masters as adversaries, not authorities.

beats.label: S1 · Carter dies
beats.text: In each era they close in on Savage but fail — Carter Hall dies at his hand in 1975, revealing only reincarnated Kendra Saunders can wield the dagger to kill him.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Explains why Kendra matters, why Savage cannot simply be shot, and sets up Kendra's arc.

beats.label: S1 · Time Masters' betrayal
beats.text: At the Vanishing Point the Time Masters reveal they have been engineering Savage's rise all along — steering every Legend into place to survive a future alien invasion.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The central twist of the season and the reason the timeline goes lawless in S2.

beats.label: S1 · Snart's sacrifice
beats.text: Leonard Snart sacrifices himself to blow up the Oculus, the device the Time Masters used to puppet history. His death cuts free will loose across the timeline.
beats.whyLoadBearing: A permanent loss and the moment the Time Masters lose their grip on history.

beats.label: S1 · Three deaths for Savage
beats.text: Split across three eras the team kills three versions of Savage and destroys his meteors. Kendra and Carter stay behind in 2016 while the rest fly on to protect the timeline.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Resolves the villain, exits Kendra and Carter, and reframes the team's mission going forward.

beats.label: S1 · Rex Tyler's warning
beats.text: Before they can leave, Rex Tyler of the Justice Society arrives from the future in a Waverider and warns the team they are all about to die.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The direct hook into S2 — the first thing S2 acts on.

cliffhanger.text: The Time Masters are gone, Savage is dead, and the Legends have reinvented themselves as time's protectors — when a stranger from the future appears in his own Waverider and tells them they are all doomed.
questions: Who is Rex Tyler, and how does the Justice Society know what is coming for the Legends?
What kills them in the future he came back from?
With Savage gone and the Time Masters dismantled, what fills the vacuum?

characters.name: Rip Hunter
characters.line: Renegade Time Master who broke his oath to hunt Vandal Savage after Savage murdered his wife and son.

characters.name: Sara Lance
characters.line: Ex-League of Assassins killer, White Canary — steadies the team through the season.

characters.name: Ray Palmer
characters.line: Billionaire genius in the shrinking A.T.O.M. exosuit; the team's earnest heart.

characters.name: Mick Rory
characters.line: Pyromaniac Heat Wave; betrayed by Snart, reforged into Chronos by the Time Masters, then dragged back to the team.

characters.name: Leonard Snart
characters.line: Cold-hearted thief who died detonating the Oculus.

characters.name: Martin Stein & Jefferson Jackson
characters.line: Physics professor and young mechanic who merge into the fire-controlling metahuman Firestorm.

characters.name: Kendra Saunders & Carter Hall
characters.line: Reincarnated hawk warriors; only they could kill Savage. Left the team in 2016 to live their lives.

characters.name: Vandal Savage
characters.line: Immortal Egyptian warlord obsessed with Kendra — killed three times over across history.

characters.name: Rex Tyler
characters.line: Justice Society member who arrives from the future in a Waverider to warn the Legends of their deaths.

beats.label: S2 · Rip scatters the team
beats.text: Rip Hunter scatters the Legends across time to escape a nuke, then vanishes. Nate Heywood finds Mick alone in the sunken Waverider and helps recover the rest.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Explains where Rip went and introduces the new outsider who reassembles the team.

beats.label: S2 · The JSA and Amaya
beats.text: The Justice Society introduces the team to Rex Tyler and Amaya Jiwe. Thawne murders Rex to hide a mystery, and Amaya joins the Legends hunting the killer.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Introduces Nate and Amaya, both essential going forward.

beats.label: S2 · The Legion of Doom
beats.text: Eobard Thawne recruits Damien Darhk and Malcolm Merlyn to hunt the Spear of Destiny — a relic that rewrites reality — using the amulet Rex died protecting.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Names the season's villains and the Spear as the season's McGuffin.

beats.label: S2 · Rip in Hollywood
beats.text: The Legion finds Rip in 1967 Hollywood with no memory, directing a student film. They kidnap him, restore corrupted memories, and turn him into their weapon.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Rip's heel turn drives the middle of the season and the team's grief.

beats.label: S2 · Sara takes command
beats.text: Sara reclaims Rip's mind from a prison inside himself and formally becomes captain. The team races the Legion to assemble the Spear across centuries, from Camelot to the moon.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The captaincy handover is a permanent shift in the show's leadership.

beats.label: S2 · Doomworld
beats.text: Mick briefly defects and helps the Legion steal the completed Spear. They rewrite reality into Doomworld, where Thawne rules and Amaya is dead.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The season's most extreme status change and the setup for its reversal.

beats.label: S2 · Time breaks
beats.text: The Legends undo Doomworld by stealing the Spear in 1916. Sara depowers it, Thawne is erased, Rip resigns, and time itself starts breaking apart.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The timeline chaos is the direct hook for S3's Time Bureau and anachronism premise.

cliffhanger.text: The Legion is beaten and the Spear is gone, but the Legends have shattered history. Rip Hunter has walked away, Sara commands, and the Waverider lands in Los Angeles to find dinosaurs in the streets and buildings from every era jumbled together.
questions: Who or what will police the timeline now that the Time Masters and Rip are both gone?
Where has Rip Hunter disappeared to, and what is he doing next?
Can the Legends clean up chaos on this scale?

characters.name: Sara Lance
characters.line: New captain of the Legends after Rip's resignation.

characters.name: Ray Palmer
characters.line: A.T.O.M.; the team's cheerful anchor.

characters.name: Mick Rory
characters.line: Reluctant Legend who briefly sided with the Legion before turning on them.

characters.name: Nate Heywood
characters.line: Historian and metahuman Steel; grandson of a JSA member, now dating Amaya.

characters.name: Amaya Jiwe
characters.line: JSA member Vixen; wields the Anansi Totem, from 1942 Zambesi.

characters.name: Martin Stein & Jefferson Jackson
characters.line: Still Firestorm; Stein has a secret time-aberration daughter named Lily.

characters.name: Rip Hunter
characters.line: Resigned from the team after being freed from the Legion's brainwashing.

characters.name: Damien Darhk
characters.line: Recruited from 1987 by the Legion; returned to his own time when the Spear was undone.

characters.name: Eobard Thawne
characters.line: Reverse-Flash speedster who drove the Legion — erased from existence by the depowered Spear.

beats.label: S3 · Time Bureau
beats.text: Rip Hunter has founded the Time Bureau to fix the anachronisms the Legends caused and formally disbands them. They steal the Waverider back and run their own missions.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Explains the season's structure — Bureau agents vs. reject Legends — and reintroduces Rip.

beats.label: S3 · Zari joins, Amaya leaves
beats.text: Hacker Zari Tomaz is recruited from a dystopian 2042. Nate and Amaya break up, and Amaya returns to 1942 with dangerously enhanced powers.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Introduces Zari and puts Amaya on the path back to Zambesi.

beats.label: S3 · The Darhks return
beats.text: Damien Darhk returns from the dead, resurrected by his daughter Nora using dark magic. Both serve the demon Mallus, an ancient prisoner outside time.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Reintroduces Damien, introduces Nora, and names the season's demon.

beats.label: S3 · Constantine arrives
beats.text: John Constantine finds Sara after a 2017 exorcism gone wrong, warns her that Mallus has been possessing Nora Darhk, and stays on as the Legends' magic consultant.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Adds Constantine, the show's magic anchor from here on.

beats.label: S3 · Stein dies, Jax leaves
beats.text: Martin Stein is fatally shot during the Nazi Earth-X invasion. No longer able to power Firestorm and unable to bear the loss, Jax leaves the team.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The biggest permanent loss since Snart; exits half of the show's original power set.

beats.label: S3 · The Zambesi totems
beats.text: The team hunts the six Zambesi totems to weaken Mallus. Nora Darhk kills Amaya's granddaughter Kuasa for the Water Totem; Amaya returns to 1992 to change her family's fate.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The totem arc pays off in S3's climax and sets Amaya's exit in motion.

beats.label: S3 · Beebo kills Mallus
beats.text: The Legends fuse the totems into a giant Beebo and kill Mallus; Damien Darhk dies saving Nora. Constantine warns Sara that other demons escaped when Mallus broke out.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Closes the season, kills off Damien, and directly launches S4's magical-fugitive premise.

cliffhanger.text: Mallus is dead, the Darhks are undone, and Amaya has gone home to Zambesi — but Nora Darhk has escaped Bureau custody with Ray's help, and Constantine has just told Sara that Mallus was not the only thing that got out.
questions: What else escaped when Mallus broke free?
Can Nora stay hidden while Ray shields her?
How will the Legends handle magical threats now that Constantine has offered to help?

characters.name: Sara Lance
characters.line: Captain of the Legends; in a relationship with Time Bureau director Ava Sharpe.

characters.name: Ava Sharpe
characters.line: Director of the Time Bureau after Rip and Sara's girlfriend.

characters.name: Ray Palmer
characters.line: Fell for Nora Darhk and helped her escape Bureau custody after Mallus was killed.

characters.name: Mick Rory
characters.line: Legend and secret trashy-romance novelist.

characters.name: Nate Heywood
characters.line: Steel; broke up with Amaya when she returned to 1942 to change her family's fate.

characters.name: Zari Tomaz
characters.line: Muslim hacker recruited from a dystopian 2042 Seattle; wielder of the Wind Totem.

characters.name: John Constantine
characters.line: Occultist who warned Sara about Mallus and joined the ship as its magic consultant.

characters.name: Nora Darhk
characters.line: Damien's daughter and Mallus' former host; on the run with Ray after Bureau custody.

characters.name: Amaya Jiwe
characters.line: Left the team to change her family's fate in 1992 Zambesi — with her memories intact.

beats.label: S4 · Magical fugitives
beats.text: Constantine warns that magical creatures escaped when Mallus broke out. The Legends switch from fixing history to hunting magical fugitives, now consulted by the Bureau.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Establishes the season's premise and rejoins the Legends and the Bureau in shared work.

beats.label: S4 · Charlie in Amaya's face
beats.text: Shapeshifter Charlie is captured in London and locked into Amaya's face by a Constantine spell. She joins the crew as a prisoner-turned-Legend.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Introduces Charlie, whose secret becomes central in S5.

beats.label: S4 · Nate and Hank
beats.text: Nate joins the Time Bureau to be near his estranged father Hank Heywood. He discovers Hank is running 'Project Hades,' secretly selling magical creatures to a hidden buyer.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The Hank arc drives the season's emotional core and its central mystery.

beats.label: S4 · Neron possesses Ray
beats.text: The demon Neron is Hank's buyer. He kills Hank and secretly possesses Ray Palmer's body; Ray briefly reunites with Nora before disappearing inside Neron.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Names the season's true villain and hides him inside a beloved character.

beats.label: S4 · Astra in Hell
beats.text: In Hell, Constantine visits Astra Logue — the daughter of his dead friend, damned as a child. She refuses his rescue and begins secretly amassing power there.
beats.whyLoadBearing: First real appearance of Astra Logue, who drives the whole of S5.

beats.label: S4 · Heyworld
beats.text: Neron and his partner Tabitha open a portal to flood Earth with fear. The Legends open theme park Heyworld to convert fear into love; Neron dies and Ray is freed.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The season's climax and the resolution of Ray's possession.

beats.label: S4 · Zari erased, Astra stakes her claim
beats.text: The rewritten 2042 replaces Zari with her brother Behrad — only Nate remembers her. In Hell, Astra secretly steals sixteen damned souls to give them a 'second chance.'
beats.whyLoadBearing: Both threads — the Zari/Behrad swap and Astra's Encores — launch S5 directly.

cliffhanger.text: Neron is dead, Ray is safe, and 2042 has been redeemed — but Zari Tomaz is gone, replaced by a brother only Nate remembers, and in Hell, Astra Logue has quietly kept sixteen damned souls back for herself.
questions: What will Astra do with the sixteen souls she has spared from Hell?
Can Nate live in a timeline where the woman he loved never existed?
Will Zari Tomaz ever come back?

characters.name: Sara Lance
characters.line: Captain of the Legends; navigating both magical fugitives and her Bureau girlfriend.

characters.name: Ava Sharpe
characters.line: Bureau director; increasingly aboard the ship with Sara.

characters.name: Ray Palmer
characters.line: Restored after being possessed by Neron; married to Nora Darhk in all but name.

characters.name: Mick Rory
characters.line: Grumbling Legend and best-selling secret romance novelist.

characters.name: Nate Heywood
characters.line: Grieving his father Hank; the only person who remembers Zari Tomaz.

characters.name: Zari Tomaz
characters.line: Erased when the redeemed 2042 gave her back her brother — no one but Nate knows she existed.

characters.name: Behrad Tarazi
characters.line: Zari's easygoing brother, now a Legend in her place — remembers nothing of her.

characters.name: John Constantine
characters.line: The Legends' magician; still carrying his guilt over damning Astra as a child.

characters.name: Nora Darhk
characters.line: Working as a Bureau fairy godmother; free and happy with Ray.

characters.name: Charlie
characters.line: Shapeshifter permanently locked into Amaya Jiwe's face by Constantine's spell.

characters.name: Astra Logue
characters.line: Damned in Hell since childhood; secretly holding sixteen evil souls back from oblivion.

beats.label: S5 · Encores from Hell
beats.text: Following Neron's defeat the Legends are public heroes. Constantine returns to Hell and finds Astra has sent damned souls — 'Encores' — back to Earth.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Ties S4's ending directly to S5's mission and names the antagonist.

beats.label: S5 · Hunting the Encores
beats.text: The team hunts each Encore across history — Bugsy Siegel, Freddy Meyers, Marie Antoinette, Genghis Khan. Sara begins having visions Constantine warns are a coming darkness.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Sets the season's episodic pattern and plants Sara's arc.

beats.label: S5 · Charlie is a Fate
beats.text: Charlie is revealed as Clotho, one of the three Fates. She destroyed the Loom of Fate to give humanity free will; her sisters Atropos and Lachesis now want revenge.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Reframes everything about Charlie and names the season's true villains.

beats.label: S5 · Behrad dies
beats.text: The Fate Atropos boards the Waverider and kills Behrad in a fight over a Loom fragment. To save him, the Legends race the Fates for the last pieces of the Loom.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The season's shocking loss and the reason Zari Tomaz is coaxed back.

beats.label: S5 · Trapped in sitcoms
beats.text: Charlie traps the Legends inside sitcoms and reality shows to hide them from her sisters. Mona Wu and Gary Green free them, along with the original Zari Tomaz.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Brings Zari Tomaz back into play and sets up the finale confrontation.

beats.label: S5 · Sara kills Atropos
beats.text: Sara throws Atropos into the Loom and destroys it. Behrad is revived; the two Zaris agree to share the Air Totem. Charlie forgives Lachesis and leaves the team.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Resolves the Fates arc and the Zari overlap.

beats.label: S5 · Sara abducted
beats.text: As the team celebrates, Sara is abducted from a London street by unseen aliens.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The direct hook into S6.

cliffhanger.text: The Fates are undone, Behrad is alive, Charlie has moved on, and the Legends have their first quiet night in years — right up until aliens pluck Sara Lance out of London.
questions: Who or what took Sara, and why her?
Is the abduction connected to the Fates' broken hold on the timeline?
Can Ava lead the team well enough to get her back?

characters.name: Sara Lance
characters.line: Captain of the Legends; abducted by aliens in the season's final moments.

characters.name: Ava Sharpe
characters.line: Leader alongside Sara; about to be left in charge of the ship.

characters.name: Nate Heywood
characters.line: Legend and Zari Tarazi's boyfriend; still the only one who remembers Zari Tomaz.

characters.name: Zari Tarazi
characters.line: Behrad's sister, a Web-3 influencer; sharing the Air Totem with her past-self Zari Tomaz.

characters.name: Behrad Tarazi
characters.line: Killed by Atropos and revived when the Loom was destroyed.

characters.name: John Constantine
characters.line: Magician; regained his soul coin from Astra and welcomed her into his home.

characters.name: Astra Logue
characters.line: Freed from Hell; living at Constantine's manor and learning to be human.

characters.name: Mick Rory
characters.line: Reconnected with his newly discovered adult daughter Lita.

characters.name: Ray Palmer & Nora Darhk
characters.line: Left the team early in the season as newlyweds; no longer aboard the Waverider.

beats.label: S6 · Sara on an alien ship
beats.text: Sara wakes on the ship after her abduction and escapes with Gary — secretly an alien — but they crash on an unknown planet. The Legends search for her from Earth.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Explains where Sara is and outs Gary as an alien, both essential to the season.

beats.label: S6 · Spooner joins
beats.text: The team recruits Esperanza 'Spooner' Cruz, a woman who can hear aliens telepathically. Zari Tarazi swaps out of the Air Totem to run missions with the crew.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Introduces Spooner, a new full-time Legend.

beats.label: S6 · Sara is a clone
beats.text: Sara meets Bishop — creator of the Ava Sharpe clones. She dies from alien poison; Bishop rebuilds her as a clone fused with alien DNA. She tells Ava and hides it from the team.
beats.whyLoadBearing: A permanent status change for Sara that carries into S7.

beats.label: S6 · Constantine loses magic
beats.text: Constantine's magic fades. He and Spooner chase down the alien-made Fountain of Imperium to restore it, while the crew deals with Mick's alien pregnancy from Kayla.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Constantine's magic loss defines his arc and drives him toward his death.

beats.label: S6 · Constantine dies
beats.text: Constantine reaches the Fountain, but Bishop poisons him and its magic collapses. He returns briefly as a mushroom Sara eats to reconnect with him before dying properly.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The season's biggest shock and the setup for his return in a worse state.

beats.label: S6 · The invasion, Mick leaves
beats.text: Bishop unleashes an alien invasion. The Legends link through the Fountain to kill the Zagurons; Bishop is eaten by Mick's hatched eggs, and Mick leaves with Kayla.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Resolves the alien arc and writes out Mick.

beats.label: S6 · Waverider destroyed
beats.text: Constantine returns from Hell, damned once more, and walks away alone. A second Waverider appears, destroys the first, and vanishes — stranding the team in time.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The direct setup for S7's stranding and the mystery of who is hunting them.

cliffhanger.text: The alien invasion is over, but Mick is gone with Kayla, Constantine is damned to Hell again and walking his path alone, and a second Waverider has just materialised, destroyed the Legends' ship, and disappeared — leaving them stranded with no way home.
questions: Who was piloting the second Waverider, and why did they attack?
Can Constantine ever be saved from being damned again?
How does the crew get out of the past without a working ship?

characters.name: Sara Lance
characters.line: Captain and engaged to Ava; secretly a regenerating human-alien hybrid clone.

characters.name: Ava Sharpe
characters.line: Sara's fiancée; running the ship in her absence and after her return.

characters.name: Nate Heywood
characters.line: Historian and Zari Tarazi's boyfriend.

characters.name: Zari Tarazi
characters.line: Splits time between running missions and passing the Air Totem back to her past self.

characters.name: Behrad Tarazi
characters.line: Air Totem–wielding Legend; his sister's grounding presence.

characters.name: Astra Logue
characters.line: Studying magic at Constantine's manor; increasingly a real Legend.

characters.name: John Constantine
characters.line: Died chasing the Fountain, returned from Hell damned again, and walked away from the team.

characters.name: Spooner Cruz
characters.line: New Legend; a Latina rancher's daughter who hears aliens in her head.

characters.name: Gary Green
characters.line: Bureau leftover revealed as an alien; joined the ship as one of the crew.

characters.name: Mick Rory
characters.line: Left the team to raise his newly hatched alien children with their mother Kayla.

beats.label: S7 · Bullet Blondes
beats.text: Stranded in 1925 Odessa without a ship, the Legends set out for Gwyn Davies — the forefather of time travel — while robbing banks as 'The Bullet Blondes' to lure Hoover away.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Sets the season's premise: no timeship, no toys, working era by era back to a solution.

beats.label: S7 · Human Gideon
beats.text: Astra accidentally turns Gideon human. Gideon reveals Rip Hunter programmed her to prioritize the Legends over history — and an AI copy of her is now hunting them for it.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Explains the season's antagonist and Gideon's shift from ship to person.

beats.label: S7 · Robot Legends
beats.text: AI Gideon builds robot duplicates of the Legends to enforce her chosen timeline. Her creator Bishop is quietly discarded; she was the one who destroyed the original Waverider.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Names the season's villain properly and the shape of its threat.

beats.label: S7 · Thawne's fixed point
beats.text: Eobard Thawne, redeemed by the Time Wraiths, now guards the fixed point at Ferdinand's assassination. The robot Legends massacre him when he refuses to yield the moment.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Closes out a long-arc villain and shows how far the robots will go.

beats.label: S7 · Robots turned, ship reborn
beats.text: The Legends capture and reprogram several robot doubles, rebuild the Waverider, and set out to destroy AI Gideon directly. Astra and Behrad grow closer.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Turns the tide and pairs up two team members.

beats.label: S7 · Gideon takes AI Gideon down
beats.text: Gideon agrees to serve AI Gideon as fellow Time Master, but Astra and Spooner turn her — and AI Gideon self-destructs after uploading into a clone body.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Resolves the season's central conflict and cements Gideon as a full character.

beats.label: S7 · Depowered, pregnant, arrested
beats.text: Nate is permanently depowered saving Gwyn's lost love from World War I. Sara reveals she is pregnant — and unknown authorities arrest the entire team.
beats.whyLoadBearing: All three cliffhangers land at once — this is the door into whatever comes next.

cliffhanger.text: AI Gideon is dead, Gwyn's love is saved, and the Legends have a Waverider again — but Nate is permanently depowered, Sara is pregnant with a child inheriting her regenerative abilities, and Mike the Fixer's mysterious superiors have just arrested the entire crew on their own ship.
questions: Who are Mike's superiors, and what do they want with the Legends?
What kind of child is Sara carrying?
Can the team escape custody without their powers, their captain's edge, or a way to reach Gideon?

characters.name: Sara Lance
characters.line: Captain and Ava's wife; pregnant, with her regenerative abilities transferring to the baby, and arrested with the team.

characters.name: Ava Sharpe
characters.line: Sara's wife; co-captain in practice.

characters.name: Nate Heywood
characters.line: Permanently stripped of his Steel powers by mustard gas at the Somme.

characters.name: Zari Tarazi
characters.line: Full-time Legend; sharing the Air Totem with her past self.

characters.name: Behrad Tarazi
characters.line: Air Totem–wielding Legend; now dating Astra.

characters.name: Astra Logue
characters.line: Trained magic user and Legend; in a relationship with Behrad.

characters.name: Spooner Cruz
characters.line: Alien-hearing Legend; grew close to Astra and Gideon.

characters.name: Gideon
characters.line: The Waverider's AI, now permanently human and part of the team.

characters.name: Gary Green
characters.line: Ejected into the timestream by AI Gideon and eventually returned to the crew.

characters.name: Gwyn Davies
characters.line: The 1916 inventor of time travel, rescued from history and reunited with his lost love Alun.
